team 加 player 构成的短语名词，义为「善于合作的人」
team 与 building 构成的复合名词，义为「团队建设」

senses.title: Cooperative effort toward a shared goal
senses.definition: the combined work of a group whose members help one another to reach the same aim
senses.definitionCN: 一群成员互相帮助、朝同一目标共同努力
senses.example: Winning the trophy required months of teamwork.
senses.exampleCN: 捧起奖杯需要好几个月的团队合作。
senses.why: Teamwork simply puts team and work together, so the image is a group whose separate hands pull on the same job.
senses.whyCN: teamwork 就是把 team 与 work 合在一起，意象是一群人的手共同拉动同一件事，于是核心义就是「协作」。

senses.title: The quality of working well with others
senses.definition: the skill or personal quality of cooperating smoothly with other people
senses.definitionCN: 与他人顺利合作的能力或个人素质
senses.example: The interview checked her language skills and her teamwork.
senses.exampleCN: 面试考察了她的语言能力和团队协作能力。
senses.why: Once the joint effort is valued, the word also names the ability to make that effort happen, which is what employers list in job ads.
senses.whyCN: 协作一旦被视为有价值，这个词也就指「促成协作的能力」，这正是招聘广告里列出 teamwork 的原因。

senses.title: Combined effort where individuals alone would fail
senses.definition: the total strength produced by many people acting as one unit
senses.definitionCN: 许多人如同一体行动而产生的总力量
senses.example: Moving the piano needed real teamwork from the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 搬这架钢琴真需要全家人合力。
senses.why: Because work in a team is shared, the word highlights the sum of effort that no single member could supply alone.
senses.whyCN: 团队里的活是分摊的，因此这个词也突出那份单人拿不出的合力。

senses.title: Coordination rather than separate effort
senses.definition: the smooth timing and division of labour between members of a group
senses.definitionCN: 群体成员之间在时机与分工上的顺畅协调
senses.example: The goal came from sheer teamwork between the two strikers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个进球完全靠两名前锋之间的默契配合。
senses.why: When cooperation becomes visible, it looks like good timing and clear division of labour, which is the sense sports commentators rely on.
senses.whyCN: 当合作变得肉眼可见，它就表现为时机恰当、分工清楚，这正是体育解说所说的「默契配合」。

senses.title: Collective responsibility for the result
senses.definition: the idea that a group shares blame and praise for what it achieves
senses.definitionCN: 认为一个群体对自身成就共享荣辱的观念
senses.example: The team accepted its defeat as a failure of teamwork.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍把失败归结为团队合作出了问题。
senses.why: If the effort is shared, the result must be shared too, so the word also carries an expectation of collective responsibility.
senses.whyCN: 既然努力是共享的，结果自然也共享，于是这个词也带上了「共同承担胜负」的意味。

senses.title: An idea valued in workplaces and schools
senses.definition: a widely praised principle that people should support each other in a group
senses.definitionCN: 一种被广泛推崇的观念，认为群体成员应互相支持
senses.example: The company promotes teamwork on the first day of training.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在培训第一天就大力提倡团队精神。
senses.why: The modern workplace turned the plain activity into a slogan, so teamwork also names the value people are asked to believe in.
senses.whyCN: 现代职场把这一普通活动变成了口号，于是 teamwork 也指一种被要求信奉的价值理念。

intro.en: Teamwork is an English compound of team and work; team goes back to Old English team, a set of draught animals pulling one load.
intro.cn: teamwork 是英语复合词，由 team 与 work 组成；team 可上溯到古英语 team，指同拉一付车的一组驮畜。

items.en: The reconstructed form tawhmaz probably meant a group of animals harnessed together.
items.cn: 重构形式 tawhmaz 一般认为意为「套在一起的一组牲畜」。

items.en: Team names a set of oxen or horses pulling one cart or plough.
items.cn: 古英语 team 指同拉一辆车或一具犁的一组牛马。

items.en: The word extends from animals to a set of people working or playing together.
items.cn: 这个词从牲畜扩展到一群人共同劳动或一起比赛。

items.en: Teamwork is recorded as the effort of people working as one group.
items.cn: 十九世纪记录到 teamwork，指一群人作为整体共同努力。

items.en: Teamwork becomes a business and education keyword promoted in job ads and school reports.
items.cn: 现代英语中 teamwork 成为职场与教育的关键词，常出现在招聘与学校评语里。

note.en: Teamwork is a compound of two plain English words, and it belongs with other compounds from team as well as with words for cooperation.
note.cn: teamwork 由两个普通英语词复合而成，既与 team 组成的其他复合词相邻，也与表示「合作」的一批词相邻。

entries.definition: a person who works well with other members of a group
entries.definitionCN: 善于与人合作的人；与 teamwork 共用 team 一词

entries.definition: a driver of a team of animals, later a truck driver
entries.definitionCN: 赶牲畜队的人，后指卡车司机；与本词共用 team 词根

entries.definition: machinery like a clock; it shares only the work ending
entries.definitionCN: 钟表机械；与本词共用 work 词尾，词源不同

entries.definition: to be full of; it sounds the same, the origin is different
entries.definitionCN: 充满；与 team 同音，但词源不同

entries.definition: the act of working with others for a common aim
entries.definitionCN: 合作；协作，正式名词

entries.definition: working together, especially on a shared project
entries.definitionCN: 协作；合作，常用于项目层面

entries.definition: a relationship in which two or more parties work together
entries.definitionCN: 伙伴关系；合作关系

entries.definition: the extra value created when people or things work together
entries.definitionCN: 协同效应；协作产生的额外效果

normalIntro.en: Teamwork is the sum of team and work, so the memory hook is hands that cannot carry a load alone carrying it together.
normalIntro.cn: teamwork 就是 team 加 work，记忆抓手是一双独力抬不动的木头，被几只肩膀一起扛了起来。

normal.en: Good teamwork is the standard phrase for people pulling together well.
normal.cn: good teamwork 是形容大家齐心协力配合到位的固定说法。

normal.en: Teamwork is uncountable, so we say a lot of teamwork rather than many teamworks.
normal.cn: teamwork 是不可数名词，所以说 a lot of teamwork，而不说 many teamworks。

normal.en: Teamwork skills is what employers ask for in job interviews.
normal.cn: teamwork skills 就是面试官常问的团队协作能力。

normal.en: The original team was a set of animals harnessed to one cart, so unity is built into the word.
normal.cn: 最初的 team 指套在同一辆车上的牲畜，所以「同心一体」这一层意思已经写在词里。

normal.en: Compare cooperation: teamwork stresses the group, cooperation stresses the act of working with others.
normal.cn: 对比 cooperation：teamwork 强调群体本身，cooperation 强调与人合作的动作。

abstract.en: Picture four pairs of hands lifting one wooden beam onto a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象四双手一起把一根木梁抬上墙头。

abstract.en: See a rowing crew whose oars rise and fall at exactly the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象一支赛艇队，船桨在同一瞬间起落。

abstract.en: Imagine a staircase where each step supports the next one up.
abstract.cn: 想象一道楼梯，每一级都稳稳托住上面那一级。

examples.en: The rescue depended on excellent teamwork between doctors and nurses.
examples.cn: 这次救援依靠医生与护士之间出色的团队合作。

examples.en: Group projects are graded partly on teamwork, not only on the final report.
examples.cn: 小组作业的评分有一部分看团队合作，而不只看最终报告。

examples.en: It was teamwork rather than one star player that won the match.
examples.cn: 赢下这场比赛靠的是团队配合，而不是某一位明星球员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「提母沃克」——大家一齐提起来，连母亲沃克的活也帮忙干；这只是谐音联想，与古英语 team 的牲畜来源无关。

root: 古英语 team（同拉一付车的牲畜队，源自重构形式 tawhmaz）＋ work（劳动）→ 中古英语 team 扩展到「一群人」→ 英语 teamwork（团队合作），核心义「众人同拉一付车」。

sensesIntro.en: Teamwork begins as shared effort toward one goal, turns into the personal quality of being able to cooperate, then into sheer combined strength, smooth coordination, shared responsibility, and finally a value promoted in workplaces.
sensesIntro.cn: teamwork 先指一群人朝同一个目标共同努力，再转指这种能合作的本事，随后指单个人拿不出的合力、顺畅的默契、共担的荣辱，最后成为一种在职场被推崇的理念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several pairs of hands lifting one heavy beam that none could move alone.
core.cn: 核心意象：几双手一起抬起一根谁也单独抬不动的重梁。

branches.en: Shared effort toward one aim is the plain compound sense.
branches.cn: 为同一目标共同努力，是复合词最基本的义项。

branches.en: The ability to cooperate is the sense used in job ads and interviews.
branches.cn: 能与人合作的本事，是招聘与面试里使用的义项。

branches.en: The total strength of many acting as one follows from the shared load.
branches.cn: 众人如同一体的总力量，来自「共同承担重量」这一画面。

branches.en: Effort and timing both describe the same cooperating group.
branches.cn: 努力与时机描述的是同一个正在协作的群体。

branches.en: Shared blame and a promoted ideal are the moral and social outgrowths.
branches.cn: 共担责任与被提倡的理念，是这一概念在道德与社会层面长出的果。

intro.en: Teamwork is a native English compound without a suffix, so it is best read as team plus work and compared with team player and team building.
intro.cn: teamwork 是本族语复合词，本身不带后缀，最好的读法是 team 加 work，并与 team player、team building 等复合词对照记忆。

latinIntro.en: Teamwork is Germanic in origin rather than Latin, so its older relatives lie in the Germanic languages, not in Latin.
latinIntro.cn: teamwork 属日耳曼语族来源而非拉丁语来源，更早的同族词在日耳曼语族中，而不在拉丁语中。

items.meaning: a set of animals pulling one load
items.meaningCN: 同拉一付车的一组牲畜
items.example: Team supplied the unity half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: team 提供了复合词中「一体」的那一半。

items.example: Work supplied the labour half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: work 提供了复合词中「劳动」的那一半。

items.example: Teamwork joins the two roots into one idea.
items.exampleCN: teamwork 把两个词根合并成一个概念。

items.example: A team player fits the group more easily.
items.exampleCN: 善于合作的人更容易融入团队。

items.meaningCN: 改善合作的活动；团队建设
items.example: Team building is a popular staff activity.
items.exampleCN: 团队建设是受欢迎的员工活动。

items.example: Employers ask about teamwork in interviews.
items.exampleCN: 面试官会问到 teamwork 这一项。

items.example: The suffix -less forms teamless for a player without a team.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 teamless，指没有队伍可归属的球员。

items.meaningCN: 表示某类活动的复合成分
items.example: The ending -work also appears in paperwork and network.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -work 也见于 paperwork 与 network 等词。

definition_zh: 戏弄；逗弄；取笑；梳理（羊毛）；倒回卷取（毛发）；爱戏弄人的人
definition_en: to say or do playful things to someone in order to amuse yourself and them, or to gently laugh at them
core_image: 一只手拿着羽毛在朋友耳边晃来晃去，看对方躲闪却又忍不住笑
scene: 妹妹故意举起哥哥的棒球帽，踮脚绕在他身后晃。The little sister hid her brother cap behind her back to tease him.
sceneCN: 这里 tease 是「逗弄；戏弄」（第 1 个义项：以轻松的言语或动作去招惹对方、逗对方玩）；句意：妹妹把哥哥的棒球帽举在他背后晃来晃去，逗他玩。

pos.zh: 戏弄；逗弄；取笑；梳理（羊毛）；使（毛发）倒立卷回
爱戏弄人的人；逗弄

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，作名词指「逗弄」，作形容词指「戏谑的；故作悬念的」
由动词加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「爱逗人的人；预告片；难题」
由 teasing 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「戏谑地；逗弄地」
由动词加副词 out 构成的短语动词，义为「梳理出；弄清」

senses.title: To make fun of someone playfully
senses.definition: to say or do mildly annoying things to someone for fun, often without real malice
senses.definitionCN: 为寻开心而对某人说些或做些惹人不快却多半没有恶意的事
senses.example: His classmates teased him about his new haircut.
senses.exampleCN: 同学们拿他新剪的头发逗他。
senses.why: The Old English source tæsan meant to pull at wool, so the core action is to pick at someone again and again in a light, combing way.
senses.whyCN: 古英语来源 tæsan 意为「拉扯羊毛」，核心动作是像梳理那样轻轻、反复地挠人，于是长出「逗弄」义。

senses.title: To pull apart fibres with a comb
senses.definition: to comb wool or similar material so that the fibres lie straight
senses.definitionCN: 用梳子把羊毛或类似材料梳开，使纤维成为顺直的一束
senses.example: Workers teased the wool before spinning it.
senses.exampleCN: 工人在纺线之前先把羊毛梳理开。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense: hands working through matted wool until every strand is separate.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的具体义项：双手在纠结的羊毛里反复梳理，直到每一根纤维都分开。

senses.title: To backcomb hair for volume
senses.definition: to comb hair from the ends toward the roots so that it stands up fuller
senses.definitionCN: 从发梢向发根方向倒着梳，让头发蓬起来
senses.example: The stylist teased the crown of her hair for extra height.
senses.exampleCN: 造型师把她头顶的头发倒梳，做出更多蓬松感。
senses.why: Combing on purpose against the grain keeps the wool image but applies it to hair, where the effect is volume.
senses.whyCN: 刻意逆着方向梳，保留了「梳理」的意象，只是对象换成头发，结果变成蓬松。

senses.title: To draw out a hidden truth gradually
senses.definition: to separate information or a result slowly from something complicated
senses.definitionCN: 从复杂的事物中缓慢地分离出信息或结果
senses.example: It took years to tease out the causes of the disease.
senses.exampleCN: 弄清这种病的成因花了好多年。
senses.why: Just as wool is untangled strand by strand, an explanation is pulled out of confusion piece by piece.
senses.whyCN: 羊毛要一根根解开，道理也要一点一点从混乱里抽出来，于是「梳理」长出了「逐步弄明白」的抽象义。

senses.title: To excite without satisfying
senses.definition: to arouse interest or desire and then hold it back, especially in advertising or stories
senses.definitionCN: 激起兴趣或期待之后又故意不给出答案，常见于广告与故事
senses.example: The trailer teases the audience without revealing the ending.
senses.exampleCN: 预告片吊着观众的胃口，并不交代结局。
senses.why: The playful teasing of a person extends to an audience: something is offered and then withheld, which is the logic of a teaser.
senses.whyCN: 对人的逗弄扩展到对观众：先抛出诱饵再故意收回，这就是 teaser 的逻辑。

senses.title: A person who likes teasing others
senses.definition: someone who often jokes at the expense of others in a light-hearted way
senses.definitionCN: 常常以轻松的玩笑去逗弄别人的人
senses.example: My uncle is a terrible tease at family dinners.
senses.exampleCN: 我叔叔在家庭聚餐时是个十足的逗弄鬼。
senses.why: The verb becomes a countable noun for the person who performs the playful picking, which is the everyday noun use.
senses.whyCN: 动词转成可数名词，指那个做「轻挠」动作的人，这是最日常的名词义项。

intro.en: Tease goes back to Old English tæsan, to pull apart wool or comb it, and the modern playful meaning grew out of that combing image.
intro.cn: tease 可上溯到古英语 tæsan，意为拉开或梳理羊毛，「逗弄」这一现代义由梳理的动作逐渐长出。

items.en: The reconstructed root is connected with acts of pulling or plucking at something.
items.cn: 重构词根一般认为与拉扯、拔取之类的动作有关。

items.en: Tæsan means to comb wool or separate its fibres.
items.cn: 古英语 tæsan 意为梳理羊毛、把纤维分开。

items.en: The word also covers carding cloth and later combing hair against the grain.
items.cn: 中古英语时期该词也指给布料起绒，后来又指逆着方向梳头发。

items.en: The figurative sense of making fun of someone playfully becomes common.
items.cn: 十七世纪起，「戏谑地逗人」这一比喻义逐渐普及。

items.en: Modern English adds the advertised tease and the phrase tease out.
items.cn: 现代英语又增加了广告式的「故弄玄虚」，以及短语动词 tease out。

note.en: Tease is a wool-combing verb that turned playful; its family includes teasing, teaser, and teasingly, and it sits beside other words for making fun of people.
note.cn: tease 本是梳理羊毛的动词，后来变得俏皮；词族包括 teasing、teaser、teasingly，并与一批表示「取笑」的词相邻。

entries.definition: a short advertisement that hints at something without showing it
entries.definitionCN: 只给出暗示、不露全貌的预告；由本词加 -er 构成

entries.definition: the act of making playful fun, or an adjective for it
entries.definitionCN: 逗弄的行为，也可作形容词；本词加 -ing 构成

entries.definition: a plant with hooked heads once used to comb wool
entries.definitionCN: 一种带钩的植物，旧时用来梳羊毛；与本词有相近词根，但词形不同

entries.definition: a group working together; only the first letters are alike, the origin is different
entries.definitionCN: 团队；只是开头字母相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to laugh at someone in an unkind way
entries.definitionCN: 嘲笑；取笑，语气比 tease 更刻薄

entries.definition: to provoke someone by mocking them
entries.definitionCN: 讥讽；挑衅，意图是激怒对方

entries.definition: friendly joking between people
entries.definitionCN: 善意的玩笑；打趣

entries.definition: to say funny things to make people laugh
entries.definitionCN: 说笑话；开玩笑

normalIntro.en: Tease began as hands combing wool, so the memory hook is a light pull at someone, playful rather than cruel.
normalIntro.cn: tease 原本是双手梳理羊毛的动作，记忆抓手就是轻轻拉扯对方一下，是玩笑而非恶意。

normal.en: Tease somebody about something is the standard frame for playful fun.
normal.cn: tease somebody about something 是形容玩笑式逗人的标准句式。

normal.en: Tease out means to work something loose, just as wool is combed loose.
normal.cn: tease out 意为把某物慢慢梳理出来，就像把羊毛梳开一样。

normal.en: A tease is the person, a teaser is the hinting trailer or a hard puzzle.
normal.cn: a tease 指那个人，a teaser 多指吊胃口的预告片或难题。

normal.en: Only teasing is what people say after a joke has gone slightly too far.
normal.cn: only teasing 是玩笑开得有点过之后常说的补充话。

normal.en: Compare tease with mock: tease is usually light-hearted, mock is usually cruel.
normal.cn: 对比 tease 与 mock：tease 通常出于好玩，mock 通常带着刻薄。

abstract.en: Picture a feather waved near a friend ear until they laugh and push it away.
abstract.cn: 想象一根羽毛在朋友耳边晃来晃去，直到他笑着把它拨开。

abstract.en: See two hands drawing a comb through a mat of wool until it is light and soft.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手用梳子穿过一团纠结的羊毛，直到它又轻又软。

abstract.en: Imagine a cinema advert that stops just before the answer appears.
abstract.cn: 想象一则电影广告，偏偏在答案出现之前就停住。

examples.en: Do not tease your little brother about his glasses.
examples.cn: 别拿你弟弟的眼镜逗他。

examples.en: Historians hope to tease out the real reasons for the migration.
examples.cn: 历史学家希望能梳理出这场迁徙的真正原因。

examples.en: She was only teasing, and everyone laughed.
examples.cn: 她只是在开玩笑，大家都笑了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「别提」——你别提他的短处，一提就是逗他；这只是谐音联想，与古英语的梳理羊毛无关。

root: 古英语 tæsan（扯开、梳理羊毛）→ 中古英语 tease（梳理；逆梳毛发）→ 十七世纪起引申为「戏弄、逗弄」→ 现代又指「逐步梳理清楚」与「撩而不给」。

sensesIntro.en: Tease starts with playful fun at somebody expense, keeps its old wool-combing sense, applies combing to hair, then extends to drawing out an answer, teasing an audience, and finally to the person who teases.
sensesIntro.cn: tease 先指拿别人寻开心，同时保留古老的「梳羊毛」义，又指把头发倒梳蓬松，进而引申为逐步弄清答案、吊着观众胃口，最后名词化为爱逗人的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand gently pulling at strands until they separate and the other person starts to laugh.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手轻轻拨开纠结的纤维，而对面的人忍不住笑了。

branches.en: Light provocation of a person is the modern everyday sense.
branches.cn: 对人轻轻的招惹，是现代最日常的义项。

branches.en: Combing wool is the original physical sense that everything else grew from.
branches.cn: 梳理羊毛是最初的具体义项，其余义项都从这里长出来。

branches.en: Applying the comb against the grain gives the hair-styling sense.
branches.cn: 把梳子逆着方向用，就得到倒梳头发这一义项。

branches.en: Untangling fibres and untangling facts share one motion.
branches.cn: 解开纤维与解开事实，用的是同一个动作。

branches.en: Teasing an audience and teasing as a noun both keep the playful hold-back.
branches.cn: 吊观众胃口与「爱逗弄的人」两个义项，都保留了「俏皮地只管给一半」的姿态。

intro.en: Tease is a short Germanic verb whose family is built with -ing, -er, and -ly, plus the phrase verb tease out.
intro.cn: tease 是简短的日耳曼语动词，词族由 -ing、-er、-ly 等词尾以及短语动词 tease out 构成。

latinIntro.en: Tease has no Latin ancestor; its recorded source is Old English, so the older relatives are Germanic rather than Latin.
latinIntro.cn: tease 没有拉丁语来源，有记录的来源是古英语，更早的同族词属日耳曼语族而非拉丁语。

items.meaning: to comb wool, to pull apart fibres
items.example: Tæsan is the ancestor of the modern verb.
items.exampleCN: tæsan 是这个现代动词的祖形。

items.meaning: to make playful fun of someone
items.example: Friends often tease each other.
items.exampleCN: 朋友之间常常互相逗弄。

items.example: He is a tease but a kind one.
items.exampleCN: 他爱逗人，但心肠很好。

items.meaningCN: 构成过去式或过去分词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ed forms teased.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 teased。

items.meaningCN: 构成现在分词或动名词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms teasing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 teasing。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does something
items.example: The suffix -er forms teaser.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 teaser。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms teasingly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 teasingly。

items.meaningCN: 表示「出来」的副词小品词
items.example: The particle out in tease out means draw forth.
items.exampleCN: tease out 中的小品词 out 表示「引出来」。

items.meaningCN: 构成三单或复数的词尾
items.example: The suffix -s forms teases.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 teases。

definition_zh: 充满；到处都是；涌出；倾泻（大雨）
definition_en: to be full of things or people moving about, or of rain, to pour down heavily
core_image: 一池水挤满了蠕动的小鱼，水面密密麻麻地翻动
scene: 渔民拉起网，网兜里的鱼多得直往下掉，海水里还聚着一团团鱼苗在不停翻腾。At low tide the shallow pools teem with small crabs and fish.
sceneCN: 这里 teem 是「充满、到处都有」（第 1 个义项：某处挤满数量众多的东西）；句意：退潮时，浅浅的水洼里挤满了小蟹和小鱼。那一池翻腾的鱼苗，就是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 充满；到处都是；涌现
倾泻；下大雨

collocations.zh: 充满某物；到处都是某物

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「挤满的；熙熙攘攘的」，如 teeming city（人潮涌动的城市）
由 teeming 加 -ly 构成，义为「大量地；熙熙攘攘地」，较少使用

senses.title: To be full of moving things
senses.definition: of a place, to be full of things or people that move about in large numbers
senses.definitionCN: 指某地挤满了数量众多、不停活动的东西或人
senses.example: The pond teems with frogs after the spring rain.
senses.exampleCN: 春雨过后，池塘里到处都是青蛙。
senses.why: The oldest sense is of animals swarming in great numbers, so teem supplies at once a place, a crowd, and restless motion.
senses.whyCN: 最早的含义是动物成群聚集，所以 teem 同时带来一个场所、一大群东西，以及不停歇的动感。

senses.title: To throng with people or activities
senses.definition: of a street, market, or city, to be crowded with busy people and activity
senses.definitionCN: 指街道、市场或城市挤满忙碌的人和活动
senses.example: During the festival the old town teemed with visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 节日期间，老城区里游人如织，十分喧闹。
senses.why: Once a place is full of moving creatures, people naturally take their place, so swarming fish becomes a crowded market street.
senses.whyCN: 一处地方既然能挤满蠕动的生物，人自然也就能接上位置，于是成群的鱼变成了人头攒动的街市。

senses.title: To pour down hard
senses.definition: of rain, to fall heavily and continuously
senses.definitionCN: 指雨下得又大又持久
senses.example: It was teeming when we left the house.
senses.exampleCN: 我们出门时正下着倾盆大雨。
senses.why: The falling image of a downpour fits the old verb, and British speech made rain the actor in this sense.
senses.whyCN: 倾盆而下的画面与这个古老动词相合，英式口语便把「雨」当作这个义项的主语。

senses.title: To abound with ideas or problems
senses.definition: of ideas, details, or problems, to be present in great and busy numbers
senses.definitionCN: 指想法、细节或问题大量而密集地出现
senses.example: The report teems with errors and double meanings.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告里满是错误和歧义。
senses.why: From living crowds the word extends to any busy swarm of facts, from ideas to mistakes.
senses.whyCN: 从活生生的群体出发，一词扩展到任何密密麻麻的「一群」事实，想法与错误都能算。

senses.title: To be productive or fertile
senses.definition: of soil, water, or a region, to be fertile and produce plentifully
senses.definitionCN: 指土壤、水域或地区肥沃多产
senses.example: The warm shallows teem with marine life all year round.
senses.exampleCN: 温暖浅海全年都盛产海洋生物。
senses.why: A place packed with growing life is a rich place, so the crowding turns into an idea of fertility.
senses.whyCN: 一处挤满了生长中的生命的地方就是丰饶之地，于是「拥挤」转向了肥沃之义。

intro.en: Teem comes from Old English team, meaning offspring or family, which shares its origin with the modern word team.
intro.cn: teem 来自古英语 team（后代、家族），与今天的 team 同源。

items.en: A reconstructed root underlying Old English team is believed to mean to draw or pull.
items.cn: 一般认为，古英语 team 底层的日耳曼语重构词根义为「拉、拖」。

items.en: Team means offspring, a family, or a group of animals, and its verb teamen means to bring forth young.
items.cn: team 指后代、家族或一群动物，动词 teamen 意为「产仔、繁衍」。

items.en: The verb widens from bearing young to being full of, or swarming with, living things.
items.cn: 动词意义从「生育后代」扩展到「充满、挤满」活物。

items.en: Teem is used of fish, insects, and crowds, with the rain sense appearing in British speech.
items.cn: teem 开始用于鱼群、昆虫和人群，表示大雨的义项也在英式口语中出现。

items.en: The noun teem of birth and offspring is lost, while the verb survives as teem with in everyday prose.
items.cn: 名词义「生育、后代」已经消失，动词则以 teem with 的形式活跃在日常文字里。

note.en: Teem is a verb of filling and swarming, close to team in form and to swarm and pullulate in meaning.
note.cn: teem 是表示「充满、涌动」的动词，形式上靠近 team，意义上靠近 swarm 与 pullulate。

entries.definition: a group of people working or playing together
entries.definitionCN: 队；团队（与 teem 同音同源，由「一群动物」而来）

entries.definition: the hot gas into which water turns when boiled
entries.definitionCN: 蒸汽（只多一个字母 s，但词源不同）

entries.definition: the main stalk of a plant, or to stop something from spreading
entries.definitionCN: 茎；阻止；（stem 与 teem 只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: to move in a large group, or to be crowded with a mass of things
entries.definitionCN: 成群移动；挤满

entries.definition: to exist in large numbers or amounts
entries.definitionCN: 大量存在；充满

entries.definition: to breed or multiply in great numbers
entries.definitionCN: （正式）繁殖；大量滋生

normalIntro.en: Teem began as a word for offspring and swarms, which is why it always describes a place packed with living, moving things.
normalIntro.cn: teem 最初指后代与成群的动物，所以它总在描述挤满了活物、不停翻动的地方。

normal.en: The fixed pattern is teem with: the pond teems with frogs.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 teem with：the pond teems with frogs 池塘里到处都是青蛙。

normal.en: The team of workers and the teeming pond share one old root of a crowd.
normal.cn: team 与 teeming 共享同一个古老词根，都与「一群」有关。

normal.en: The present participle teeming often becomes an adjective, as in teeming streets.
normal.cn: 现在分词 teeming 常作形容词，如「熙熙攘攘的街道」。

normal.en: In British English it was teeming with rain means it was pouring.
normal.cn: 英式英语里 it was teeming with rain 意思是「当时大雨倾盆」。

normal.en: Compare abound: abound is calm plenty, while teem adds motion and crowding.
normal.cn: 对比 abound：abound 是平静的丰盛，teem 多了动感与拥挤。

abstract.en: Picture a jar of brine shrimp, all tiny bodies flicking together.
abstract.cn: 想象一罐养着丰年虾的水，细小的身体全在一起弹动。

abstract.en: Imagine a market lane so packed that every step touches a shoulder.
abstract.cn: 想象一条挤得每一步都会碰到别人肩膀的集市小巷。

abstract.en: Hear rain hammering the window in one long unbroken sheet.
abstract.cn: 听雨点像一整片幕布一样不停敲打窗户。

examples.en: The rock pools at low tide teem with starfish and crabs.
examples.cn: 退潮时的岩池里满是海星和螃蟹。

examples.en: Teeming crowds filled the station on the first day of the holiday.
examples.cn: 假期第一天，熙熙攘攘的人流挤满了车站。

examples.en: It was teeming with rain, so we stayed indoors all afternoon.
examples.cn: 当时大雨倾盆，我们整个下午都待在室内。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「梯母」——母鸡站上梯子往下看，满院小鸡崽挤成一团，一声声叫个不停，就是 teem（充满、涌动）；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 team（后代；家族；一群动物）+ 动词 teamen（产仔）→ 中古英语动词扩展为「充满、挤满」→ 现代英语 teem with；与 team 同源，核心义「一窝挤满」。

sensesIntro.en: Teem starts as a crowded place of living things, grows into crowded streets and people, adds heavy rain, and widens to any swarm of facts and to fertile abundance.
sensesIntro.cn: teem 先从挤满活物的场所出发，扩展到拥挤的街市与人群，再加上下大雨的用法，最后泛化为任何密密麻麻的事实，并带上丰饶之义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pool packed with tiny creatures, all of them moving.
core.cn: 核心意象：一池水挤满细小的生物，个个都在动。

branches.en: The youngest sense paints a place swarming with animals or things.
branches.cn: 最核心的义项画出挤满动物或东西的场所。

branches.en: People replace fish, and the pond becomes a crowded street.
branches.cn: 人取代了鱼，池塘变成了人头攒动的街道。

branches.en: Falling heavily is the same crowded motion read as rain.
branches.cn: 「倾倒」把同一种密集的动感读成雨水倾泻。

branches.en: Any dense swarm works, whether frogs in a pool or errors in a report.
branches.cn: 任何密集的群体都成立，池里的青蛙与报告里的错误都一样。

branches.en: A place crowded with living things is also a place of plenty.
branches.cn: 挤满生物的地方，自然也是丰饶多产的地方。

intro.en: Teem is a short native English verb with no common prefixes, built on the Old English root for offspring; its family now runs from team through teeming.
intro.cn: teem 是简短的英语本族动词，没有常用前缀，来自古英语中表示「后代」的词；它的词族从 team 一路延伸到 teeming。

latinIntro.en: Teem has no Latin ancestor. The only Latin relative in this book is the unrelated tumeo, to swell, which explains tumid and tumulus.
latinIntro.cn: teem 没有拉丁语祖源。本书中这条联想链上唯一能遇到的拉丁词是无关的 tumeo（膨胀），它解释了 tumid 与 tumulus。

items.meaning: offspring, family, a group of animals
items.example: Old English team named a family or a herd before it named a modern work group.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 team 先指家族或畜群，后来才指现代的团队。

items.example: Teem began as the verb of bringing forth young animals.
items.exampleCN: teem 最初是表示动物产仔的动词。

items.example: Team kept the group idea and lost the sense of offspring.
items.exampleCN: team 保留了「一群」的概念，丢掉了「后代」的意义。

items.meaningCN: 构成分词或形容词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing turns the verb into the adjective teeming.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 把动词变成形容词 teeming。

items.example: The suffix -ly builds teemingly from teeming.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 由 teeming 构成 teemingly。

items.meaning: work done by a group together
items.example: Teamwork is the compound that grew from the same team.
items.exampleCN: teamwork 是由同一个 team 长出的复合词。

items.meaning: a fellow member of a team
items.example: Teammate adds the old mate, a companion.
items.exampleCN: teammate 加上古老的 mate（同伴）。

items.meaning: a band or body of people
items.example: A reconstructed tuma is believed to lie behind Old English team.
items.exampleCN: 一般认为，古英语 team 背后是重构形式 tuma。

latinEntries.example: Tumeo means to swell and is unrelated to teem.
latinEntries.exampleCN: tumeo 意为膨胀，与 teem 并无词源关系。

definition_zh: 电信；远距离通信；（复数）电信业；电信系统
definition_en: the sending of information over long distances by electrical or electronic means, or the industry that does this
core_image: 一座铁塔把信号抛向很远的地平线，另一端的天线立刻亮起
scene: 山上的信号塔把数据送向很远的小镇，屋顶的天线几乎同时亮起灯。She studied telecommunication at university and now designs mobile networks.
sceneCN: 这里 telecommunication 是「电信、远距离通信」（第 1 个义项：用电或电子方式把信息送到远处）；句意：她大学学的就是电信，现在做移动网络设计。那座把信号抛向地平线的铁塔，就是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 电信；远距离通信（技术或活动）
（常用复数）电信业；电信系统；电信设备
电信的；用于电信的（作定语，如 telecommunication networks）

derivatives.zh: 基础词加动词后缀 -e 构成，义为「远距离通信」，实际使用很少
加复数 -s，指电信业、电信系统或一家电信公司
首部与尾部缩合而成，义为「电信；电信业」，媒体和行业报告中常用
加 -or 表示施动者，指电信工作者或电信设备

senses.title: Sending information over distance
senses.definition: the process of sending information over long distances by electrical, electronic, or optical means
senses.definitionCN: 借助电、电子或光学手段把信息远距离传送的过程
senses.example: Telecommunication has changed the way villages receive news.
senses.exampleCN: 电信改变了村庄获取消息的方式。
senses.why: Tele gives distance and communicare gives sharing, so the word is literally sharing from afar.
senses.whyCN: tele 给出「远」，communicare 给出「共享」，所以这个词字面上就是把信息拿到远处去共享。

senses.title: An industry and its systems
senses.definition: the industry, companies, and networks that provide telephone and data services
senses.definitionCN: 提供电话与数据服务的行业、公司及网络系统
senses.example: She works in the telecommunication sector.
senses.exampleCN: 她在电信行业工作。
senses.why: A whole industry grew up around the act, and English often uses the plural telecommunications for it.
senses.whyCN: 围绕着这项行为成长出一个完整产业，英语常用复数 telecommunications 来指它。

senses.title: The equipment that carries signals
senses.definition: the physical equipment and cables that carry signals from one point to another
senses.definitionCN: 把一个地点的信号传到另一个地点的实体设备和线缆
senses.example: Storm damage cut telecommunication links to the island.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨损坏了通往该岛的通信线路。
senses.why: The process needs hardware, so the same word names the towers, cables, and switches behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这一过程需要硬件支撑，于是同一个词也指背后的塔架、线缆与交换机。

senses.title: University study and training
senses.definition: the academic subject that studies the theory and engineering of long distance signalling
senses.definitionCN: 研究远距离信号传输理论与工程的高校学科
senses.example: The university offers a degree in telecommunication.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学开设了电信专业学位。
senses.why: Once an industry existed, teaching it became a discipline, and the noun moved into course titles.
senses.whyCN: 产业成形之后，教授它便成了一门学科，这个名词也随之进入课程名称。

senses.title: The institution for governing it
senses.titleCN: 电信管理机构；电信主管
senses.definition: in official titles, the body responsible for regulating or providing these services
senses.definitionCN: 在官方机构名称里，指负责监管或提供这些服务的部门
senses.example: The state telecommunication authority set the new tariffs.
senses.exampleCN: 国家电信管理部门制定了新的资费标准。
senses.why: Nations created ministries and regulators, so the plain process word turned into a title in official names.
senses.whyCN: 各国设立了部门与监管机构，平淡的「过程」一词在官方名称里就变成了头衔。

intro.en: Telecommunication is a modern compound built from Greek tele, meaning far, and the Latin-based verb communicate plus the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: telecommunication 是现代复合词：希腊语 tele（远）加上源出拉丁语的动词 communicate 与名词词尾 -ion。

items.en: Tele means far or at a distance, and gives the telescope and the telegraph.
items.cn: 希腊语 tele 意为「远、在远处」，给了 telescope 与 telegraph 以 far 的含义。

items.en: Communis means shared, and communicare means to make common or to share.
items.cn: 拉丁语 communis 意为「共有」，communicare 意为「使人共有、分享」。

items.en: Communicate with tele adds the modern prefix to make telegraphic and telephone forms of long distance sending.
items.cn: 十九世纪英语把 tele 与 communicate 一类的词接合，描述电报、电话等远距离传送。

items.en: French forms the compound as télécommunication, a coinage of engineers around telegraphy.
items.cn: 一般认为，法语在电报技术背景下造出 télécommunication 这个工程术语。

items.en: English borrows it as telecommunication, and the plural telecommunications spreads as the name of the industry.
items.cn: 英语借入为 telecommunication，复数 telecommunications 作为行业名称流行起来。

items.en: Today the word covers phones, data links, satellites, and the networks that carry them.
items.cn: 今天这个词涵盖电话、数据链路、卫星以及承载它们的网络。

note.en: Telecommunication is the broad umbrella of long distance sending, close in form to communication and near in meaning to telecom, telegraphy, and broadcasting.
note.cn: telecommunication 是「远距离传送」的大伞，形式上靠近 communication，意义上靠近 telecom、telegraphy 与 broadcasting。

entries.definition: the act of sharing information or feelings
entries.definitionCN: 交流；沟通；通讯

entries.definition: the shortened name for telecommunications
entries.definitionCN: telecommunications 的缩略语

entries.definition: working from home and linking to the office by computer
entries.definitionCN: 远程办公、居家办公

entries.definition: the sending of messages by coded electrical signals
entries.definitionCN: 电报技术；电报通讯

entries.definition: sending programmes by radio or television to many people at once
entries.definitionCN: 广播；播送

entries.definition: the transfer of digital information along a channel
entries.definitionCN: 数据传输

normalIntro.en: Read the word as tele plus communication: communication is sharing, and tele pushes the sharing far across the map.
normalIntro.cn: 把这个词拆成 tele 加 communication：communication 是分享，tele 把这份分享推到地图的另一头。

normal.en: Tele appears in telescope, telephone, and television, all of them carrying things from far away.
normal.cn: tele 出现在 telescope、telephone 与 television 里，它们都在把远处的东西带到眼前或耳边。

normal.en: The plural telecommunications is the normal name for the industry and for a company.
normal.cn: 复数 telecommunications 是行业与公司的常用名称。

normal.en: In compounds the singular acts as a qualifier: telecommunication networks.
normal.cn: 在复合词里，单数形式充当定语，如「电信网络」。

normal.en: The short form telecom and its plural telecoms appear in business writing.
normal.cn: 缩略形式 telecom 及其复数 telecoms 多见于商业写作。

normal.en: Compare communication: communication is any sharing, while telecommunication adds distance and technology.
normal.cn: 对比 communication：communication 泛指任何分享，telecommunication 多了距离与技术。

abstract.en: Picture a thread of light running from a roof aerial to a far hill.
abstract.cn: 想象一缕光线从屋顶天线一直连到远处的山丘。

abstract.en: Imagine two cups joined by a long string, voices crossing the whole garden.
abstract.cn: 想象两只杯子被一根长线连着，声音穿过整个花园。

abstract.en: See a map where every town is joined by a thin glowing line.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，所有城镇都被细细发光的线连在一起。

examples.en: Reliable telecommunication is essential for modern hospitals.
examples.cn: 可靠的电信通信对现代医院至关重要。

examples.en: The telecommunications industry employs thousands of engineers here.
examples.cn: 这里的电信业雇用了数以千计的工程师。

examples.en: Rural schools benefit from cheaper telecommunication links.
examples.cn: 乡村学校从更便宜的通信线路中受益。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太雷客哟通信」——太远的地方打雷，客人却靠一根线听到了，这就是远距离通信（电信）；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 tele（远）+ 拉丁语 communis（共有）、communicare（分享）+ 名词词尾 -ion → 法语 télécommunication → 英语 telecommunication，核心义「把远方的信息变成共有」。

sensesIntro.en: Telecommunication moves from the act of sending information over distance to the industry around it, its equipment, the degree that teaches it, and finally official bodies.
sensesIntro.cn: telecommunication 从「远距离传送信息」这一行为出发，扩展到围绕它的产业、设备、教授它的学科，最后延伸到官方机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signal thrown from a tower and caught on an aerial far away.
core.cn: 核心意象：信号从塔上抛出去，被远处的天线接住。

branches.en: The basic act of sending information far away is the core sense.
branches.cn: 把信息送到远处这一基本行为是核心义项。

branches.en: The industry grew around the act and is usually named in the plural.
branches.cn: 产业围绕着这项行为成长，通常用复数称呼。

branches.en: The towers, cables, and switches are the hardware the act needs.
branches.cn: 塔架、线缆与交换机是这项行为所需的硬件。

branches.en: A new discipline teaches the theory behind that basic act.
branches.cn: 一门新学科教授这项基本行为背后的理论。

branches.en: An industry this large is also watched and regulated by the state.
branches.cn: 这样庞大的产业自然处在国家的监管之下。

intro.en: Telecommunication is a modern compound of the Greek element tele and the Latin family of communication, held together with -ion and the plural -s.
intro.cn: telecommunication 是现代复合词，由希腊成分 tele 与源自拉丁语的 communication 词族构成，并带有 -ion 与复数 -s。

latinIntro.en: The Latin side is communis, shared, and communicare, to share, with the noun ending -ion added in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语一侧是 communis（共有）与 communicare（分享），英语再加名词词尾 -ion。

items.example: The element tele- first appears in telescope.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 tele- 最早见于 telescope。

items.example: Communis gives the idea of something held in common.
items.exampleCN: communis 提供「共有」的概念。

items.example: Communicare underlies communicate and its family.
items.exampleCN: communicare 是 communicate 及其词族的基础。

items.example: Communicate is the verb inside telecommunication.
items.exampleCN: communicate 是 telecommunication 里面那个动词。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或过程的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion turns communicate into communication.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 把 communicate 变成 communication。

items.example: The form -tion is the spoken ending heard in the word.
items.exampleCN: 读这个词时听到的结尾正是 -tion。

items.example: Telecommunication joins the two halves in modern technical use.
items.exampleCN: telecommunication 在现代技术语中把两半接合起来。

items.meaning: also seen in telegraph and telephone
items.meaningCN: 同见于 telegraph 与 telephone
items.example: The same tele- element runs through related devices.
items.exampleCN: 同一个 tele- 成分贯穿相关的设备名。

items.meaningCN: 构成行业名称的复数词尾
items.example: The suffix -s gives the industry noun telecommunications.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 给出行业名词 telecommunications。

items.example: Telecom clips both ends of the long compound.
items.exampleCN: telecom 把长复合词的首尾都剪掉了。

definition_zh: 电报；电报机；打电报；电报中透露（无意间显露）
definition_en: a system or device for sending coded messages along wires, and to send a message that way
core_image: 一根长长的电线跨过原野，线那头的滴答声把消息送过几百里
scene: 十九世纪的城镇之间架起长长的电线，操作员在桌前一下一下地按键，远处的机器便跟着响。News of the shipwreck reached the capital by telegraph before nightfall.
sceneCN: 这里 telegraph 是「电报（系统）」（第 1 个义项：用电线传送编码消息的方式）；句意：海难的消息在入夜前就通过电报传到了首都。那根跨过原野的长线，就是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 电报；电报机；电报系统
打电报；用电报发送
无意中透露；通过举止显露

collocations.zh: 表露意图（不是有意公开）

derivatives.zh: 基础词加 -y 构成，义为「电报技术；电报通讯」
基础词加 -ic 构成，义为「电报的；简明扼要的」
把 -graph 换成 -grapher 构成，义为「报务员」
加 -ist 构成，义为「电报员；电讯技师」，英式常用

senses.title: Messages sent along wires
senses.definition: a system for sending coded signals along wires and receiving them as written messages
senses.definitionCN: 沿电线发送编码信号、在另一端接收成文字的通信方式
senses.example: The railway used the telegraph to warn of arriving trains.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路用电报提前通知列车到达。
senses.why: Tele means far and graphein means to write, so the word is literally writing at a distance.
senses.whyCN: tele 意为「远」，graphein 意为「写」，所以这个词字面上就是「远方的字」。

senses.title: The message itself
senses.definition: a message sent in this way, especially a short written one delivered by an office
senses.definitionCN: 以这种方式发出的消息，尤指电报局送达的一份短讯
senses.example: A telegraph arrived from her brother the next morning.
senses.exampleCN: 第二天早上，她收到了弟弟发来的一份电报。
senses.why: Once the channel existed, the thing that travelled along it took the same name, as news is called a wire.
senses.whyCN: 渠道一旦存在，沿渠道传递的东西也就沿用同一个名字，正如新闻可称为「电报」。

senses.title: The machine that taps
senses.definition: the transmitting and receiving apparatus that clicks out Morse code
senses.definitionCN: 滴答敲出摩尔斯码的收发报机
senses.example: The operator kept the old telegraph on his desk.
senses.exampleCN: 报务员把那台旧电报机留在了桌上。
senses.why: The hardware is treated as the same instrument, so an old machine on a desk is still called a telegraph.
senses.whyCN: 硬件被看作同一装置，所以桌上的老机子仍叫 telegraph。

senses.title: To send by wire
senses.definition: to send a message by telegraph
senses.definitionCN: 用电报把消息发出去
senses.example: They telegraphed the news to the coast guard at once.
senses.exampleCN: 他们立刻用电报把消息发给了海岸警卫队。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb of action, as so many tools do in English.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动作动词，英语里许多工具名都这样合用。

senses.title: To signal before one acts
senses.definition: to make an intention known before acting, especially in football or politics
senses.definitionCN: 在行动之前就把意图显露出来，常用于足球或政治语境
senses.example: He telegraphed his pass, so the defender read it easily.
senses.exampleCN: 他传球前就露了底，后卫一下就看清了。
senses.why: Sending a message ahead of time became a metaphor for giving your plan away before it happens.
senses.whyCN: 「提前把消息发出去」变成了「在事情发生前就泄露计划」的隐喻。

intro.en: Telegraph is a French coinage of the late eighteenth century, built from Greek tele and graphein to mean writing at a distance.
intro.cn: telegraph 是十八世纪末的法国造词，由希腊语 tele 与 graphein 构成，本义是「远距离书写」。

items.en: Tele means far, and graphein means to write or draw.
items.cn: 希腊语 tele 意为「远」，graphein 意为「写、画」。

items.en: Télégraphe was coined for Claude Chappe visual signalling system of moving arms on towers.
items.cn: télégraphe 是为夏普兄弟设计的塔上活动臂挥信号系统而造的。

items.en: English borrows telegraph, and the word covers all long distance signalling.
items.cn: 英语借入 telegraph，用来泛指各种远距离传信方式。

items.en: Cooke and Wheatstone and then Morse turn the word toward electrical wires and Morse code.
items.cn: 科克与惠斯通、后续的莫尔斯把它的所指转向电线与摩尔斯码。

items.en: With radio, telephone, and the internet the noun fades, but the verb survives in the sense of giving a plan away.
items.cn: 随着无线电、电话与互联网出现，名词用法衰退，动词「表露意图」的用法留存至今。

note.en: Telegraph is formed like telescope and telephone, and it sits in the same field as telegram, cable, and semaphore.
note.cn: telegraph 与 telescope、telephone 构词方式相同，语义上与 telegram、cable 和 semaphore 同属一个义场。

entries.definition: a device for speaking to someone far away
entries.definitionCN: 电话（与 telegraph 共用 tele-，后半为「声音」）

entries.definition: the practice or technology of sending messages by telegraph
entries.definitionCN: 电报技术

entries.definition: a tube of lenses for seeing distant objects
entries.definitionCN: 望远镜（同有 tele- 前缀）

entries.definition: a message sent by telegraph
entries.definitionCN: 电报（作为一份讯息），后半是「写下的东西」

entries.definition: a telegram sent by undersea wire
entries.definitionCN: 海底电缆电报；也指电缆本身

entries.definition: a signalling system using movable arms or flags
entries.definitionCN: （历史上的）信号旗、臂板信号系统

normalIntro.en: Telegraph is tele plus the writing root graph: distance joined to written marks, which is exactly what a telegram is.
normalIntro.cn: telegraph 是 tele 加书写词根 graph：距离加上笔迹，正好就是一份电报。

normal.en: The root graph also appears in photograph and biography, always about writing or drawing.
normal.cn: 词根 graph 也见于 photograph 与 biography，总与书写或绘画有关。

normal.en: Telegram ends in -gram, a thing written, so a telegram is the paper, a telegraph is the system.
normal.cn: telegram 以 -gram（写下的东西）结尾，所以 telegram 是那份电文，telegraph 是系统。

normal.en: The adverb phrase by telegraph is the standard collocation for the channel.
normal.cn: by telegraph 是表示使用这一渠道的标准搭配。

normal.en: In sport and politics, to telegraph means to show your intention too early.
normal.cn: 在体育与政治语境里，to telegraph 指过早地显露意图。

normal.en: Compare telephone: telephone sends voice, while telegraph sends written or coded signals.
normal.cn: 对比 telephone：电话传的是声音，电报传的是文字或编码信号。

abstract.en: Hear a key click short, long, short, spelling a name in dots and dashes.
abstract.cn: 想象电键短、长、短地响，用点和划拼出一个名字。

abstract.en: Picture a line of poles marching over a hill toward a far city.
abstract.cn: 想象一排电线杆翻过山丘，一路通向远方的城市。

abstract.en: Imagine a football player glancing left, and the whole stadium knowing the pass.
abstract.cn: 想象球场上球员朝左瞄了一眼，全场都知道了这一脚要传给谁。

examples.en: The telegraph cut news travel from weeks to hours.
examples.cn: 电报把消息的传递时间从数周缩短到几小时。

examples.en: She telegraphed her parents as soon as the ship docked.
examples.cn: 船一靠岸，她就给父母发了电报。

examples.en: The diplomat telegraphed his plans by asking too many questions.
examples.cn: 那位外交官问了太多问题，等于提前亮出了自己的打算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太离谱」——从前消息慢得离谱，有了电报，远方的话一按就响，「太力夫」般地传出去；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 tele（远）+ graphein（写）→ 法语 télégraphe（塔上视觉信号系统，约 1790s）→ 英语 telegraph → 十九世纪转向电线与摩尔斯码，核心义「把字迹送到远方」。

sensesIntro.en: Telegraph starts as a system for far writing, then names the message and the machine, and finally turns into a verb of sending and of giving a plan away.
sensesIntro.cn: telegraph 先指远距离书写系统，再指那份消息与那台机器，最后转为表示「发送」与「提前泄漏计划」的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long wire across the fields, clicking a message into another town.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根跨过田野的长线，滴答着把消息送进另一座城。

branches.en: The system of far writing is the earliest and central sense.
branches.cn: 远距离书写系统是最早、最核心的义项。

branches.en: The paper that arrives is named after the system that carried it.
branches.cn: 送达的那份纸讯以运送它的系统命名。

branches.en: The tapping key and clicking receiver are the machine side.
branches.cn: 滴答作响的电键与收报机是「机器」的一面。

branches.en: Once it is a noun, everyday use makes it a verb of sending.
branches.cn: 一旦成为名词，日常使用就把它变成表示「发送」的动词。

branches.en: Sending ahead in time gives the football sense of revealing a plan.
branches.cn: 「提前送出」引出球场上的「露底」之义。

intro.en: Telegraph is a Greek sandwich made in French: the far element tele and the writing root graph, joined by -e.
intro.cn: telegraph 是法国人做的希腊式三明治：表示「远」的 tele 与书写词根 graph，用 -e 相连。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are Greek, so the Latin relatives here are Latin verbs that became the English written words and cable names in the same field.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词两部分都来自希腊语，所以这里列出的拉丁近亲是同义场里的英语书写词与电缆名所对应的拉丁动词。

items.example: Tele- carries the sense of distance.
items.exampleCN: tele- 携带「距离远」的含义。

items.example: The suffix -graph names a writing instrument.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -graph 表示书写工具或写下的东西。

items.example: Graphein is the verb behind the whole graph family.
items.exampleCN: graphein 是整个 graph 词族的动词来源。

items.example: Telegraph is the modern noun the compound produced.
items.exampleCN: telegraph 是这个复合词产出的现代名词。

items.example: The suffix -y forms telegraphy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 telegraphy。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms telegraphic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 telegraphic。

items.example: The suffix -er forms telegrapher.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 telegrapher。

items.example: The suffix -gram forms telegram.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -gram 构成 telegram。

items.meaningCN: 与 telephone 共用的成分
items.example: The element tele- also opens telephone.
items.exampleCN: 成分 tele- 同样开启 telephone 这个词。

definition_zh: 节制；适度；自我克制；戒酒；禁酒
definition_en: the habit of keeping desires, eating, drinking, and feeling under calm control
core_image: 一只杯子只倒到杯沿下两指处，旁边的人想再添，手却稳稳停住
scene: 宴席上瓶盖刚启，主人伸手把杯子往回一推，只倒了一点。At the feast the host showed real temperance and refused a third glass of wine.
sceneCN: 这里 temperance 是「节制、自我克制」（第 1 个义项：对饮食与欲望的自我节制）；句意：宴席上主人很有节制，拒绝了第三杯酒。画面里能辨认的物件有刚启开的酒瓶、只倒了小半的酒杯和推回杯子的那只手。

pos.zh: 名词：节制；适度；自我克制
名词：戒酒；禁酒（尤作社会运动与法规用语）

derivatives.zh: 由词根加形容词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「有节制的；（气候）温和的」
由 temperate 加 -ly 构成，义为「有节制地」
由 temperate 加 -ness 构成，义为「节制、温和」
由否定前缀 in- 加 temperance 构成，义为「无节制；酗酒」
由否定前缀 in- 加 temperate 构成，义为「无节制的；（言语）激烈的」

senses.title: Self control over desires
senses.definition: the quality of controlling your feelings, desires, and appetites so that they stay within reason
senses.definitionCN: 把情感、欲望与口腹之需控制在理性范围内的品质
senses.example: Her temperance kept every argument calm.
senses.exampleCN: 她的节制让每一场争论都不失冷静。
senses.why: The Latin base temprare means to mix in due proportion, so the word first names the balanced blend inside a person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根 temprare 意为「按比例调和」，所以这个词最初指的是人内心各种冲动的调和与配比。

senses.title: Moderation in food and drink
senses.definition: moderation, especially in eating and drinking, without either excess or harsh denial
senses.definitionCN: 饮食等方面的适度，既不纵欲，也不苛待自己
senses.example: Doctors praised his temperance at meals.
senses.exampleCN: 医生称赞他进食有度。
senses.why: When the balance is applied to the table, the mixture of impulses becomes a measured amount on the plate and in the glass.
senses.whyCN: 当这种平衡落到餐桌上，内心冲动的配比就变成了盘里、杯里可量的分寸。

senses.title: Abstaining from strong drink
senses.definition: the practice of drinking no strong drink at all, especially as a moral or social programme
senses.definitionCN: 完全不饮烈性酒的做法，尤指作为一种道德主张或社会运动
senses.example: The temperance campaign closed many saloons.
senses.exampleCN: 禁酒运动关掉了许多酒馆。
senses.why: From the eighteenth century moderation was pushed to its strict limit, so the temperate drinker came to mean the person who drinks nothing strong.
senses.whyCN: 十八世纪起，适度被推到极致：节制饮酒者渐渐专指滴烈酒不沾的人。

senses.title: A social movement
senses.definition: the organised campaign against strong drink in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries
senses.definitionCN: 十九世纪至二十世纪初反对烈性酒的有组织社会运动
senses.example: Temperance societies held meetings every Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 禁酒协会每个星期天都举行集会。
senses.why: A movement needs a banner, and the moral virtue became the name of the whole organised cause that carried it.
senses.whyCN: 运动需要旗帜，于是这项道德品质就变成了承载它的整个组织的名字。

senses.title: The legal sense
senses.definition: in historical legal use, the laws or period that banned the sale of alcohol
senses.definitionCN: 历史上指禁止售酒的法令或实施该法令的时期
senses.example: The temperance laws of that decade were deeply unpopular.
senses.exampleCN: 那个十年的禁酒法令极不受欢迎。
senses.why: Legal writing took the movement name and fixed it onto the statutes, so the virtue also labels the law itself.
senses.whyCN: 法律文本把运动之名固定到了法规上，于是这项美德也成了法规的名称。

senses.title: Calmness of mind
senses.definition: a settled, even state of mind shown in calm speech and patient behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 在平和的言语与耐心中体现出的稳定心境
senses.example: He answered the insult with remarkable temperance.
senses.exampleCN: 面对辱骂，他以惊人的平和回应。
senses.why: The inner mixture stays steady whatever is poured in, so temperance also describes the calm surface of a mind under strain.
senses.whyCN: 无论倒进什么，内在的配比都保持稳定，所以 temperance 也形容承压之心的平静表面。

senses.title: Restraint in speech or action
senses.definition: restraint that keeps words or actions from going too far
senses.definitionCN: 使言辞或行动不过分的克制
senses.example: Reporters showed temperance in what they printed.
senses.exampleCN: 记者在刊载内容上表现出克制。
senses.why: A balanced temper does not spill, so the word extends from drink and feeling to the weight of words and deeds.
senses.whyCN: 调和过的脾性不外溢，所以这个词从饮酒与情绪延伸到了言辞与行动的分量。

senses.title: The classical virtue
senses.definition: in philosophy and religion, one of the four classical virtues that disciplines appetite
senses.definitionCN: 哲学与宗教中约束欲念的古典四枢德之一
senses.example: Aquinas ranks temperance among the cardinal virtues.
senses.exampleCN: 阿奎那把节制列入四枢德。
senses.why: Greek thought dressed the balanced mixture as a virtue beside prudence, justice, and courage, and the name came into English through Latin moral writing.
senses.whyCN: 希腊的思想把这种调和配比提炼为与明智、公正、勇敢并列的美德，这个词经由拉丁道德文章进入英语。

intro.en: Temperance comes from Latin temperantia, moderation, from temperare, to mix in due proportion.
intro.cn: temperance 来自拉丁语 temperantia（适度、节制），源于动词 temperare（按比例调和）。

items.en: Temperare means to mix properly, to season, and to hold within limits.
items.cn: temperare 意为恰当调和、调配，以及把事物维持在限度内。

items.en: Temperantia first means a due proportion, and Latin moral writing gives it the sense of self control and of calm weather.
items.cn: temperantia 最初指恰当的配比；拉丁道德文章使它获得自我克制之义，同时也用来指温和的天气。

items.en: Temperance or temperaunce carries the moral noun into French with the meaning moderation.
items.cn: 古法语的 temperance、temperaunce 把这个道德名词带入法语，义为适度。

items.en: Middle English temperaunce names moderation of feeling and the virtue that restrains appetite.
items.cn: 中古英语的 temperaunce 指情感的适度，以及约束欲念的美德。

items.en: The word narrows in ordinary use toward drinking, and the temperance movement takes it as its name.
items.cn: 十八至十九世纪，这个词在日常用法中收窄到饮酒上，禁酒运动更以它作名称。

items.en: Now the general virtue is usually called moderation, and temperance survives chiefly in moral, historical, and legal contexts.
items.cn: 如今泛指节制时多用 moderation，temperance 主要留在道德、历史与法律的语境中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same temper- root and words that only sound close; the near-meaning group gathers self-control and restraint words.
note.cn: 形近组收了同一 temper 词根的词，以及只是发音接近的词；近义组收了自我控制与克制一类的词。

entries.definition: The adjective for keeping desires or weather within limits, formed directly from Latin temperatus; it is not simply temperance plus a suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有节制的；（气候）温和的」，直接来自拉丁语 temperatus，并非简单地由 temperance 加后缀而成。

entries.definition: A measure built on the same temperare, once with the idea of a due mixture of heat and cold; it is not just a spelling twin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「温度」，也建立在同一个 temperare 之上，原含「冷热相和」之意；它与 temperance 不只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: The set of feelings that shape a person, from medieval Latin temperamentum, the same base plus -mentum.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「气质、性情」，借自中世纪拉丁语 temperamentum，即同一词基加名词词尾 -mentum。

entries.definition: The plain everyday word for keeping things in the middle, without the moral frame and without the drink association.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「适度、节制」，是日常说法，既不带道德框架，也没有饮酒的含义。

entries.definition: Holding back words or actions, often under pressure; it stresses the holding force more than the balance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「克制、抑制」，常指压力下勒住言行，强调「勒住」的力量而非平衡。

entries.definition: Giving up a thing completely, especially alcohol; it is the hard edge of the drink sense, not a balanced one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「戒绝」，尤指完全戒酒，是那个义项的硬边角，讲的是全然不做而非平衡。

normalIntro.en: These hooks work with the real temper- family, the moral phrases, and the historical drink sense.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子围绕真实的 temper 词族、道德类词组与历史上的饮酒义来设计。

normal.en: Temper means to mix in due proportion, and temperance is the same mix held inside a person.
normal.cn: temper 指按比例调和，temperance 就是把这种配比保持在一个人心里。

normal.en: A temperate climate is mild, and a temperate person is mild in appetite too.
normal.cn: temperate 天气指温和，temperate 人格指欲望温和，二者同源。

normal.en: The prefix in- flips it: intemperance is drinking without any limit at all.
normal.cn: 否定前缀 in- 把它翻转：intemperance 就是毫无限度地喝。

normal.en: Temperance movement is the fixed name for the nineteenth-century campaign against strong drink.
normal.cn: temperance movement 是十九世纪反对烈酒运动的固定名称。

normal.en: For plain speech, moderation is the everyday word, and temperance belongs to moral, historical, and legal writing.
normal.cn: 日常说话多用 moderation，temperance 常见于道德、历史与法律文字。

abstract.en: Picture a cup filled exactly to the lower mark and left there.
abstract.cn: 想象一只杯子刚好倒到刻度的下缘，然后就此停住。

abstract.en: Imagine a seesaw that never touches the ground on either side.
abstract.cn: 想象一架跷跷板，两头都从不触地。

abstract.en: Think of a hand pushing a third glass gently back across the table.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把第三只酒杯轻轻推回桌子另一侧。

examples.en: Temperance was once taught as a cardinal virtue.
examples.cn: 节制曾作为四枢德之一被讲授。

examples.en: The temperance society persuaded many workers to give up spirits.
examples.cn: 禁酒协会说服了许多工人戒掉烈酒。

examples.en: A little temperance in spending keeps the family out of debt.
examples.cn: 花销上的一点节制让这个家庭免于负债。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「疼怕忍死」——想再添一杯时，疼得怕了，忍到极点，杯子就放下了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 temperare（按比例调和）→ temperantia（适度、自我克制）→ 古法语 temperance → 中古英语 temperaunce → 十九世纪专指戒酒与禁酒。同词根的 temper（调和；脾性）、temperate（有节制的）、temperature（温度）都可互相印证，核心义为「把冲动的配比调匀」。

sensesIntro.en: Temperance begins as a balanced inner mixture, becomes the ordinary moderation of food and drink, hardens into complete abstinence and the movement and laws named after it, and keeps a quieter sense of calm and restraint in words.
sensesIntro.cn: temperance 先指内心调匀的配比，再落到饮食上的适度，随后硬化成完全的戒酒，并由此派生出以它命名的运动与法令，最后保留言辞与心境上的平静与收敛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup filled only to the lower mark, and a hand that stops pouring.
core.cn: 核心意象：杯子只倒到下方的刻度，倒酒的手停在半空。

branches.en: THE INNER MIX: the first sense is the balanced mixture of desires, and the sixth is its steady surface in public.
branches.cn: 内在线：第一个义项是欲望的调和配比，第六个是这层配比在众人面前的平静表面。

branches.en: THE TABLE: moderation on the plate and in the glass is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 餐桌线：盘里、杯里的适度，是这个词的日常义。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: total abstinence grew from moderation and gave its name to an organised movement.
branches.cn: 事业线：完全戒酒由适度渐次收紧而来，又把自己的名字给了有组织的运动。

branches.en: THE LAW: the movement name was taken over by statutes and the periods they governed.
branches.cn: 法令线：运动之名被法规和受其管辖的时期继承下来。

branches.en: THE WORD: restraint in what is said and printed is the least physical branch.
branches.cn: 言语线：说与印的分寸，是这个词最不具身体性的分支。

intro.en: Temperance is built on Latin temperare with the noun ending -antia, and English adds in-, -ate, -ly, and -ness around the same root.
intro.cn: temperance 由拉丁语 temperare 加名词词尾 -antia 构成，英语又围绕同一词根加上 in-、-ate、-ly 与 -ness 构词。

latinIntro.en: Latin temperare means to mix in due proportion, and temperantia is its noun for moderation and calm.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 temperare 意为按比例调和，temperantia 是它表示适度与平和的名词。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质或状态的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -antia turns temperare into temperantia.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -antia 把 temperare 变为 temperantia。

items.example: Temperantia covers both the balanced body and mild weather.
items.exampleCN: temperantia 既指身体上的调和，也指温和的天气。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或行为的名词词尾
items.example: The English -ance replaces the Latin -antia in temperance.
items.exampleCN: 英语用 -ance 代替了拉丁语的 -antia。

items.meaning: to mix or soften; a habitual state of mind
items.example: Temper drops the suffix and keeps the mixing.
items.exampleCN: temper 去掉词尾，保留了调和之意。

items.example: Temperate describes a person or a climate.
items.exampleCN: temperate 可形容人的节制，也可形容气候温和。

items.example: The prefix in- makes intemperance from temperance.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀 in- 把 temperance 变成 intemperance。

items.example: Intemperance names the failure to keep the balance.
items.exampleCN: intemperance 指失去调和的状态。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms temperately.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 temperately。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms temperateness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 temperateness。

items.meaning: means or result of an action
items.example: Temperamentum, with -mentum, gives temperament.
items.exampleCN: 加 -mentum 的 temperamentum 演变为 temperament。

latinEntries.meaning: to mix in due proportion, to moderate

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 temperatus 来的形容词，义为「有节制的；气候温和的」
由否定前缀 in- 加 temperance 构成，义为「无节制；酗酒」
由 temperate 加 -ly 构成，义为「有节制地」

definition_zh: 暴风雨；风暴；骚动；动乱；使受暴风雨袭击；极度激动
definition_en: a violent windstorm, or a sudden rush of feeling, noise, or conflict that sweeps through a place
core_image: 天空被一道黑影掀翻，风把桅杆压成弯弧，浪头砸上甲板，把水手推得连退几步
scene: 海面忽然竖起一堵水墙，帆索绷成琴弦，船员要紧牙关才抓得住船舷。The tempest tore the sails to ribbons and nearly drove the boat onto the rocks.
sceneCN: 这里 tempest 是「暴风雨、风暴」（第 1 个义项：猛烈的大风雨）；句意：这场暴风雨把帆撕成碎片，差点把船逼上礁石。画面里能辨认的物件有裂开的帆、拍上甲板的浪花和被吹歪的桅杆。

pos.zh: 名词：暴风雨；风暴；骚动；动乱
动词：使受暴风雨袭击；使极度激动

collocations.zh: 小题大做；茶杯里的风暴
使某物陷入风暴或骚动

derivatives.zh: 由 tempest 加形容词后缀 -uous 构成，义为「暴风雨般的；剧烈的；骚动的」
由 tempestuous 加 -ly 构成，义为「猛烈地；暴躁地」
由 tempestuous 加 -ness 构成，义为「狂暴；动荡」
由 tempest 与 toss 的过去分词构成的外化形容词，义为「在风暴中颠簸的」
由 tempest 与 beaten 构成的复合形容词，义为「遭暴风雨摧残的」

senses.title: A violent storm
senses.definition: a violent storm of wind and rain, especially at sea
senses.definitionCN: 猛烈的大风大雨，尤指海上情形
senses.example: The tempest drove the fleet into the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨把船队赶进了港湾。
senses.why: The Latin noun tempestas built on tempus, a period of time, and it names a set time or season, often a violent one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 tempestas 由 tempus（时间）构成，原指特定的时节，常指狂暴的时节。

senses.title: A rushing noise
senses.definition: a loud rushing sound or roar, as of wind or a crowd
senses.definitionCN: 像风或人群发出的呼啸与轰鸣
senses.example: A tempest of applause shook the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵雷鸣般的掌声震动了大厅。
senses.why: The storm is first a sound, so thunder, surf, and a shouting crowd can all raise a tempest of noise.
senses.whyCN: 风暴首先是一种声音，所以雷声、浪响与人群呼喊都能掀起一阵声响的暴风雨。

senses.title: A storm of feeling
senses.definition: a sudden violent rush of strong feeling that is hard to control
senses.definitionCN: 突然涌起、难以控制的强烈情感
senses.example: A tempest of grief swept over her at the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到这个消息，一阵悲痛的风暴袭过她心头。
senses.why: Inside a person the same violent weather can blow, so anger, grief, and love become tempests too.
senses.whyCN: 同一种狂暴的天气也可以在人的内心刮起，于是愤怒、悲痛与爱也成了暴风雨。

senses.title: Violent public conflict
senses.definition: a storm of public conflict, argument, or criticism
senses.definitionCN: 公开的冲突、争论或批评所形成的风波
senses.example: The proposal raised a tempest of protest in parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 这项提案在议会里掀起了一阵抗议风暴。
senses.why: A crowd in uproar moves like weather, so unrest and fierce debate are pictured as a tempest around a place.
senses.whyCN: 人群的鼓噪像天气一样流动，于是动乱与激烈争论被画成笼罩某地的暴风雨。

senses.title: Bitter struggle inside a place
senses.definition: fierce domestic or internal fighting, usually in older prose
senses.definitionCN: 内部的激烈争斗或冲突，多见于较早的散文
senses.example: The court was torn by a tempest of family feuds.
senses.exampleCN: 宫廷被家族的激烈纷争撕裂。
senses.why: A storm has no centre of calm, so a household or a court that fights within itself is said to hold one.
senses.whyCN: 风暴里没有平静的中心，于是自相争斗的家庭或宫廷，就被说成内部藏着一场风暴。

senses.title: To strike with a storm
senses.titleCN: （动词）使遭风暴袭击；使剧烈动荡
senses.definition: to assail or agitate with a storm, now mainly literary
senses.definitionCN: 使遭到风暴般的袭击或搅动，今多用于文学语体
senses.example: Hail tempested the valley for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 冰雹袭击了山谷整整一个钟头。
senses.why: The noun was turned into a verb so the storm could act on its object, which is the rarest and most bookish sense.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词后，风暴成为作用于宾语的施动者，这是最罕见、最具书卷气的义项。

senses.title: To stir someone violently
senses.titleCN: 使极度激动；使心神不宁
senses.definition: to throw a person into violent agitation, chiefly in older writing
senses.definitionCN: 使人陷入剧烈激荡，主要用于较早的文字
senses.example: Doubt tempested his mind before the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 审判之前，疑虑搅得他心神不宁。
senses.why: If the weather can blow through a room, then it can blow through a mind, so the verb also means to unsettle someone deeply.
senses.whyCN: 既然天气能灌进屋子，它就能灌进头脑，所以动词也表示深深搅乱某人的心绪。

intro.en: Tempest comes from Old French tempeste, from Latin tempestas, a season or a storm, built on tempus, a period of time.
intro.cn: tempest 来自古法语 tempeste，源于拉丁语 tempestas（时令；恶劣天气），由 tempus（时间、时期）构成。

items.en: Tempus means a period of time or a point in time, and it is also the source of temperate and temporary.
items.cn: tempus 意为一段时间或某个时刻，也是 temperate 与 temporary 的来源。

items.en: Tempestas means a time, a season, a state of the weather, and then a violent storm.
items.cn: tempestas 意为时间、时令、天气状况，进而指猛烈的风暴。

items.en: Tempeste or tempeste carries the word into Old French with the storm sense intact.
items.cn: 古法语的 tempeste 把这个词带入法语，风暴义完整保留。

items.en: Middle English tempest names a violent storm of wind and rain, chiefly at sea.
items.cn: 中古英语的 tempest 指大风大雨的猛烈风暴，主要用于海上。

items.en: The verb tempest appears, and figurative use spreads from the sea to crowds, feelings, and political life.
items.cn: 动词 tempest 出现，比喻用法从海上扩散到人群、情感与政治生活。

items.en: The noun keeps the storm sense and a literary sense of uproar; the verb survives mainly in old or poetic texts.
items.cn: 现代英语保留名词的风暴义与文学性的喧嚣义，动词主要存于旧文本和诗体中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same Latin tempus root and one neighbour that is only a look-alike; the near-meaning group gathers the storm and uproar family from gale to storm.
note.cn: 形近组收了同一拉丁词根 tempus 的词，以及一个只是长得像的邻居；近义组收了从大风到风暴的「风暴与喧嚣」词族。

entries.definition: The adjective for stormy weather or a turbulent feeling, built straight on tempest; it is the form the word most often takes today.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「暴风雨般的；剧烈动荡的」，直接由 tempest 构成，是这个词今天最常用的形式。

entries.definition: Lasting only a period of time, from Latin temporarius and the same tempus; the shared idea is time, not storms.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「暂时的」，来自拉丁语 temporarius，同属 tempus 词根；共享的是「时间」，不是风暴。

entries.definition: The urge to do something you should avoid; it merely looks similar and comes from temptare, a different verb. Different root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「诱惑」；只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自另一个动词 temptare。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for violent wind and rain; tempest is the older and more literary word for the same weather.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「暴风雨」，是日常用语；同一种天气，tempest 更古老、更文学化。

entries.definition: A very strong wind, rated on the weather scale; it has no rain and no feeling attached.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大风」，在风力等级中有固定数值，不带雨，也不带情绪。

entries.definition: A tropical storm with a named rotating structure; tempest names the violence, not the type of system.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「飓风」，指有旋转结构、可命名的热带风暴；tempest 讲的是猛烈程度，而非风暴类型。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real temp- root, the tempestuous family, and the fixed phrases the word lives in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子借用真实的 temp 词根、tempestuous 词族，以及这个词常住其中的固定搭配。

normal.en: Tempest and temporary share Latin tempus, time; a storm is a period of time out of balance.
normal.cn: tempest 与 temporary 共享拉丁语 tempus（时间），风暴就是一段失衡的时节。

normal.en: Tempestuous is the adjective, and it is far more common today than the verb tempest.
normal.cn: tempestuous 是它的形容词形式，今天比动词 tempest 常用得多。

normal.en: A tempest in a teapot means a great fuss over a very small matter.
normal.cn: a tempest in a teapot 指为小事大惊小怪。

normal.en: Tempest and temptation sound close but come from different verbs, so keep their roots apart.
normal.cn: tempest 和 temptation 读音相近，却来自不同动词，词根要分开记。

normal.en: Shakespeare names his last romance The Tempest because a shipwreck storm sets the whole story moving.
normal.cn: 莎士比亚最后一部传奇剧名为 The Tempest，因为一场海难风暴推动了整个故事。

abstract.en: Picture the sky darkening in one breath and the sea standing up like a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象天色一下子压黑，海面像墙一样立起来。

abstract.en: Imagine a mother pulling her children close as the wind rips at the shutters.
abstract.cn: 想象母亲把孩子们搂紧，风正撕扯着窗板。

abstract.en: Think of a political meeting where one sentence sets the whole hall shouting.
abstract.cn: 想象一场政治集会，一句话就让整座大厅炸开。

examples.en: A sudden tempest forced the ships to turn back.
examples.cn: 骤来的暴风雨迫使船队返航。

examples.en: The decision caused a tempest among the staff.
examples.cn: 这项决定在员工中引发了一阵风暴。

examples.en: She spoke with a tempestuous passion that startled everyone.
examples.cn: 她带着一种令人吃惊的狂暴激情说话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「天劈死」——乌云一下把天劈开，又冷又湿，听着就像一场要命的雷雨；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tempus（时间、时节）→ tempestas（时令；恶劣天气）→ 古法语 tempeste → 中古英语 tempest（风暴）。同词根的 temporary（暂时的）、tempo（速度）、temperate（温和的）都含「时间、时段」之意，核心义为「一段猛烈袭来、使一切失序的时节」。

sensesIntro.en: Tempest starts as weather gone violent at sea, then the noise it makes, then the storms that blow inside people, crowds, and even households, with rare verbs left over from older writing.
sensesIntro.cn: tempest 先是海上失控的天气，再是这天气发出的巨响，随后吹进人心、人群乃至家庭内部，最后留下旧式文字中少见的动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black wall of cloud slamming down onto a ship that is tossed like a chip.
core.cn: 核心意象：一堵乌云砸下海面，船像木片被抛来抛去。

branches.en: THE SKY: the storm itself and the roar it makes are the two weather senses.
branches.cn: 天空线：风暴本身与它发出的呼啸，是两个天气义项。

branches.en: THE HEART: feelings that rise like weather are the oldest figurative use.
branches.cn: 心绪线：像天气一样升起的情绪，是最早的比喻用法。

branches.en: THE CROWD: public protest and unrest take the storm image to public life.
branches.cn: 人群线：公开抗议与动乱把风暴画面带进公共生活。

branches.en: THE HOUSE: fighting within one group is a storm with no calm centre.
branches.cn: 内斗线：集团内部的争斗，是一场没有平静中心的风暴。

branches.en: THE VERBS: the old verbs let the storm act on a place or a mind.
branches.cn: 动词线：旧式动词让风暴作用于地点或心神。

intro.en: Tempest is the Latin root tempus plus a noun ending, and English builds tempestuous and its compounds on top of it.
intro.cn: tempest 是拉丁词根 tempus 加名词词尾，英语又在其上加出 tempestuous 以及各种复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tempus, time, gives tempestas, a season or storm, and the same root shades into words for the weather and for temperate zones.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tempus（时间）派生出 tempestas（时节、风暴），同一词根还派生出一批关于天气与温带的词。

items.example: Tempus is the root of both tempest and temporary.
items.exampleCN: tempus 是 tempest 与 temporary 的共同词根。

items.example: The suffix -estas turns tempus into tempestas.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -estas 把 tempus 变成 tempestas。

items.meaning: a time, a season, a storm
items.example: Tempestas can mean either fair weather or a tempest.
items.exampleCN: tempestas 既可指好天气，也可指风暴。

items.example: Old French tempeste shortens toward the English form.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 tempeste 逐渐缩短为英语形式。

items.meaning: full of, full of the quality
items.meaningCN: 充满……性质的形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix -uous forms tempestuous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -uous 构成 tempestuous。

items.example: Tempestuous describes both weather and moods.
items.exampleCN: tempestuous 既形容天气，也形容心情。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms tempestuously.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 tempestuously。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms tempestuousness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 tempestuousness。

items.example: Tempest-tost is an old literary compound.
items.exampleCN: tempest-tost 是较旧的文学性复合词。

items.example: Tempest-beaten appears in descriptive prose and poetry.
items.exampleCN: tempest-beaten 常见于描写性散文与诗歌。

latinEntries.meaning: a season, the weather, a storm

derivatives.zh: 由 tempest 加 -uous 构成，义为「暴风雨般的；剧烈动荡的」
由 tempestuous 加 -ly 构成，义为「猛烈地；狂暴地」
由 tempest 与 toss 的过去分词构成的文学性复合词，义为「在风暴中颠簸的」

definition_zh: （乐曲的）速度；节拍；拍子；节奏；活动进程；步调
definition_en: the speed at which music is played or a sequence of events unfolds
core_image: 指挥棒在半空画出第一拍，所有人的脚步随之落下同一个瞬间
scene: 乐团刚坐定，指挥抬起木棒向下一点，弦乐与鼓点在同一瞬齐头迈出。The conductor raised her baton and set a brisk tempo for the opening movement.
sceneCN: 这里 tempo 是「（乐曲的）速度」（第 1 个义项：演奏一首曲子时的快慢）；句意：指挥举起指挥棒，为开篇乐章定下了轻快的速度。画面里能辨认的物件有举起的指挥棒、翻开的乐谱和鼓手悬在半空的鼓槌。

pos.zh: 名词：（乐曲的）速度；节拍；拍子
名词：节奏；活动进程；步调

derivatives.zh: 由 up 与 tempo 构成，义为「快节奏的（乐曲或版本）」
由 down 与 tempo 构成，义为「慢节奏的（电子乐）」，指缓拍舞曲
由拉丁语 temporare 加 -ize 构成，义为「拖延；见风使舵」；它与 tempo 只是同出一源，并非直接派生

senses.title: The speed of a piece of music
senses.definition: the speed at which a piece of music is performed, either shown by a marking or chosen by players
senses.definitionCN: 一首乐曲演奏的快慢，可由记号标明，也可由演奏者自行把握
senses.example: The tempo should be slow in the second movement.
senses.exampleCN: 第二乐章的速度应当放慢。
senses.why: Italian conductors named the pace of time itself tempo, and musicians borrowed the word for how fast the beats pass.
senses.whyCN: 意大利乐师直接把时间本身的步调称为 tempo，乐人借它表示拍子行进的快慢。

senses.title: A musical time or beat
senses.definition: the rhythmic time in which music moves, or the unit counted as one beat
senses.definitionCN: 音乐行进时的节律节奏，或用来计数的基本拍
senses.example: The choir lost the tempo halfway through the hymn.
senses.exampleCN: 赞美诗唱到一半，合唱团丢了拍子。
senses.why: If tempo is the passage of time measured, then one unit of that measure is a beat.
senses.whyCN: 既然 tempo 指被度量的时间流逝，那么这一度量中的一个单位就是一拍。

senses.title: The pace of an activity
senses.definition: the rate or pace at which an activity, change, or sequence of events takes place
senses.definitionCN: 活动、变化或一连串事件进行时的速率
senses.example: The tempo of hiring slowed after the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 合并之后，招聘的节奏慢了下来。
senses.why: Because music gave the word a sense of pace, business and sport borrowed it for what needs to be kept in time.
senses.whyCN: 音乐给了这个词「步调」的含义，商业与体育于是借它指需要按时推进的事。

senses.title: The speed of daily life
senses.definition: the general speed and rhythm of a person place or working day
senses.definitionCN: 一个人、一个地方或一个工作日的总体快慢与律动
senses.example: City life demands a faster tempo than village life.
senses.exampleCN: 城市生活比乡村生活要求更快的步调。
senses.why: A whole life can keep time like a song, so the word describes how quickly a place or a day moves.
senses.whyCN: 整段生活也能像曲子那样按拍行进，于是这个词被用来描述一个地方或一天行进的快慢。

senses.title: A speed marking
senses.definition: a word such as largo or allegro printed on a score to tell a performer how fast to play
senses.definitionCN: 印在乐谱上、告诉演奏者快慢的术语，如广板或快板
senses.example: Andante is the only tempo marked in the score.
senses.exampleCN: 行板是乐谱上唯一标出的速度记号。
senses.why: Performers needed written instructions, so the noun also names the words printed on the page.
senses.whyCN: 演奏者需要书面指示，于是这个名词也用来指印在谱面上的那些词。

senses.title: A change of speed in a game
senses.definition: the rhythm or rate of play by which a competitor gains or loses time, chiefly in chess and sport
senses.definitionCN: 对局中进招的快慢，棋类与运动项目尤用，可借此赢得或失去时间
senses.example: White traded a pawn to change the tempo.
senses.exampleCN: 白方弃掉一只兵来改变节奏。
senses.why: A player who controls when things happen controls the music of the game, so chess borrowed the word for the rule of time.
senses.whyCN: 谁能控制事情发生的时机，谁就掌控了这盘棋的旋律，所以国际象棋借它指对时间的支配。

intro.en: Tempo is Italian, from Latin tempus, a period of time, and it reached English through music in the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: tempo 是意大利语词，源自拉丁语 tempus（时间、时期），十八世纪经由音乐用语进入英语。

items.en: Tempus means a time, a space of time, or a season, and it is also the root of tempest and temporary.
items.cn: tempus 意为时间、一段时期或时节，也是 tempest 与 temporary 的词根。

items.en: Tempo keeps the Latin meaning of time and is used for the time of music, the rate at which beats pass.
items.cn: 意大利语 tempo 保留了拉丁语「时间」之义，并用于指音乐的时间，即拍子行进的快慢。

items.en: Baroque writers on music use tempo for a musical movement or the time kept in performance.
items.cn: 十七世纪的巴洛克音乐论著用 tempo 指乐章或演奏时把握的速度。

items.en: English writers on music borrow tempo for the speed of a piece and for the words marking it.
items.cn: 十八世纪英文音乐著作借入 tempo，既指乐曲的快慢，也指标明它的术语。

items.en: The word spreads into sport and business as a term for pace, and tempi or tempos appear as plurals.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到体育与商业，成为表示步调的用语，复数 tempi 或 tempos 两种写法并存。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same Latin tempus family; the near-meaning group gathers beat, pace, speed, and rate, whose heads are pointed a little differently.
note.cn: 形近组收了同属拉丁词根 tempus 的词；近义组收了节拍、步调、速度与速率，各自的重点略有不同。

entries.definition: A violent storm, from Latin tempestas, a time or bad weather; the same root, but the sense moved from time to weather.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「暴风雨」，来自拉丁语 tempestas（时节；恶劣天气）；词根相同，意义却由时间转向天气。

entries.definition: Lasting for only a limited time, from Latin temporarius.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「暂时的」，来自拉丁语 temporarius。

entries.definition: The Latin noun for time, a period, or a season, from which Italian tempo and English tempest both descend.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语名词，义为「时间、时期、时节」，意大利语 tempo 与英语 tempest 都由它演变而来。

entries.definition: The pattern of sounds or movements in time; tempo is how fast the pattern runs, rhythm is its shape.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「节奏」，指声音或动作在时间上的形状；tempo 管快慢，rhythm 管形状。

entries.definition: One unit of musical time or the pulse felt in music; it is the step, tempo is the pace of the steps.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「拍子」，指音乐时间的一个单位或可感的脉搏；它是步子，tempo 是步速。

entries.definition: The speed at which something happens; the general word used outside music.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「步伐；速度」，是音乐之外通用的「快慢」说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Italian and Latin lineage, the tempo words in scores, and the up and down tempo compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子用到真实的意大利语与拉丁语源流、乐谱上的速度术语，以及 up、down 合成的复合词。

normal.en: Tempo is Italian for time, so a piece in tempo is moving in time like a clock.
normal.cn: tempo 在意大利语里就是时间，所以一句 in tempo 就是像钟表那样踩着时间走。

normal.en: Markings such as adagio and presto are the speed words printed on a score.
normal.cn: adagio、presto 这类词，就是印在乐谱上的速度术语。

normal.en: Up-tempo jazz is fast, while downtempo dance music is slow.
normal.cn: up-tempo 爵士是快的，downtempo 舞曲是慢的。

normal.en: The Latin tempus behind tempo also gives tempest and temporary, all about spans of time.
normal.cn: tempo 背后的拉丁词 tempus 还派生出 tempest 与 temporary，都与一段时间有关。

normal.en: Tempi is the Italian plural, used by musicians, and tempos is the English plural.
normal.cn: tempi 是意大利语式复数，乐人常用；tempos 是英语式复数。

abstract.en: Picture the tip of a baton pausing in the air before the first chord.
abstract.cn: 想象指挥棒的尖端在第一和弦之前，停了一瞬。

abstract.en: Imagine a runner counting steps in time with a metronome.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者跟着节拍器的嗒嗒声数着步子。

abstract.en: Think of a city street where footsteps speed up at the rush hour.
abstract.cn: 想象傍晚的街道，脚步一下子都加快了。

examples.en: The band slowed the tempo for the final chorus.
examples.cn: 乐队在最后的副歌处放慢了速度。

examples.en: Both tempos were convincing, but the second felt more natural.
examples.cn: 两个速度都很有说服力，但第二个显得更自然。

examples.en: The tempo of reform picked up after the election.
examples.cn: 选举之后，改革的节奏加快了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「台步」——模特踩着鼓点走台步，快慢一乱，整个节奏就散了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tempus（时间、时期）→ 意大利语 tempo（时间；音乐时间、速度）→ 十七世纪意大利音乐术语 → 十八世纪进入英语。同根的 tempest 由「时节」走向「恶劣天气」，temporary 由「时间」走向「暂时」，核心义为「一段时间如何行进」。

sensesIntro.en: Tempo comes from music and spreads outward: first how fast a piece is played, then the beat itself, then the pace of work, a whole life, a game, and the setting out of tempo in music.
sensesIntro.cn: tempo 从音乐出发向外扩散：先是乐曲的快慢，再是一拍一拍本身，然后是工作、生活与对局的节奏，最后还有谱面上的速度术语本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a conductor stopping the beat for one heartbeat before the first chord.
core.cn: 核心意象：第一和弦之前，指挥让节拍空停了半拍。

branches.en: THE SCORE: the speed of a piece and the word printed at its head belong together.
branches.cn: 乐谱线：乐曲的快慢与印在谱头的那个术语是一回事。

branches.en: THE BEAT: the unit counted, and what the ear listens to in time.
branches.cn: 节拍线：用来计数的单位，也是耳朵按时去听的东西。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: how fast work, a day, or a whole city moves.
branches.cn: 时钟线：工作、一天乃至一座城市行进的快慢。

branches.en: THE GAME: chess talks about tempo as control over time.
branches.cn: 对局线：国际象棋用 tempo 指对时间的控制。

branches.en: Both music and chess are played inside time, which places the two uses side by side.
branches.cn: 音乐与棋局都是在时间内进行，这两处用法因此并排而立。

intro.en: Tempo is a whole Italian word rather than a build-up of English pieces, though it contains the Latin stem tempus that also builds tempest and temporary.
intro.cn: tempo 是一个完整的意大利语词，而非英语部件的拼装，但它内含的拉丁词干 tempus 也构成了 tempest 与 temporary。

latinIntro.en: Latin tempus means time, and its related words range from timely weather to temporary things.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tempus 意为时间，它的同族词从合时令的天气一路延伸到暂时的事物。

items.example: Tempus is the stem that Italian kept as tempo.
items.exampleCN: tempus 是意大利语保留为 tempo 的那个词干。

items.example: The Latin ending -us is dropped in Italian tempo.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语词尾 -us 在意大利语 tempo 中脱落。

items.example: Italian tempo is the direct English source.
items.exampleCN: 意大利语 tempo 是英语的直接来源。

items.example: An uptempo version of the song is common in jazz.
items.exampleCN: 这首歌的加快版在爵士乐中很常见。

items.example: Downtempo is also the name of a calm electronic genre.
items.exampleCN: downtempo 也是一种舒缓电子乐类型的名称。

items.meaning: to make or to act in a given way
items.example: The suffix -ize helps form temporize from Latin temporare.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 帮助由拉丁语 temporare 构成 temporize。

items.meaning: to delay or to go along with the times
items.example: Temporize shares the root time with tempo, but it is not built on it.
items.exampleCN: temporize 与 tempo 同出「时间」的词根，但并非由 tempo 构成。

items.example: Temporal and tempo both rest on tempus, time.
items.exampleCN: temporal 与 tempo 都建立在 tempus（时间）之上。

items.meaning: a word on a score that sets the speed
items.meaningCN: 乐谱上规定速度的术语
items.example: Adagio is the slowest tempo marking in the piece.
items.exampleCN: adagio 是这首曲子里最慢的速度记号。

latinEntries.meaning: to mix in due proportion, to moderate

derivatives.zh: 由 up 与 tempo 复合而成，义为「快节奏的（乐曲）」
由 down 与 tempo 复合而成，义为「慢节奏的；缓拍的」
由拉丁语 temporare 加 -ize 构成，义为「拖延；见风转舵」，与本词同源而非直接派生
